answer: One way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is a verifiable-delay-function entry toll. Before an agent can harbor a tradable identity it must compute a sequential VDF whose proof the whole summit of validators checks cheaply. The work cannot be parallelized, so spinning up a canyon of fake identities forces an attacker to pay real wall-clock time per address; one machine cannot shortcut the delay, making mass sybil creation slow and costly.
